title: Expected Length of Honest Prediction Intervals in Lee Selection Models with a Saturated Stratum
banked_reason: D0.5 delivered tier incremental below field (paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4); not salvageable in current scope. Math-panel REVISE: two redundant assumptions remain unrepaired; archival result, not mathematically cleared.
gap_reasons: The delivered result establishes the explicit randomized oracle, a positive all-rule root-n lower certificate, and exact finite-sample honesty with a rule-specific Gaussian excess-length limit. [Lee's public theorem text](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02898v2) supports the cited identification inputs, leaving the contribution concentrated in learning the saturated allocation. The efficiency theorem concerns a constructed seven-coordinate family with fixed support widths and density tilts chosen so support-or-empty lotteries dominate interior thresholds; it establishes neither robustness to changing supports nor a general saturated-stratum rate theorem. Honesty over the public-floor class supplies no corresponding class-wide efficiency guarantee, and the encompassing-model transfer extends only the converse. The framing correctly distinguishes matching rate order from the allocator's performance constant and the unresolved minimax constant, so there is no stale sharp-minimax overclaim. The projected score is constrained by the specialized experiment and its limited methodological reach beyond the explicit allocation kink, rather than by the absence of matching constants or an empirical application. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

The numerical broad-retention floor pi_0>=1/40 is not consumed: positivity already follows from the cell/control/treated conditions, the global rule's broad report has zero tail, and both oracle and local converse use only the stated local family; dropping it genuinely broadens the claimed public-floor class.

The quantitative control floor p_0x>=1/100 is likewise unused beyond establishing positivity; the reproduced completion, count identities, exact-honesty proof, and local rate use only p_0x>0 (the local rectangle supplies its own uniform bound), so the global headline is stated on a gratuitously narrower class.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed the explicit randomized oracle, all-rule local root-n converse, and exactly honest count-augmentation rule, and sharpened its fixed-support upper limit to approximately 0.380828. D0.5 assessed the delivered package incremental below the field floor; the required class-wide atoms/changing-support efficiency upgrade is a new research program. The decision panel passed and citations were verified, but math-panel REVISE has two unrepaired redundant-assumption findings; no Lean formalization or mathematical clearance is claimed.
tldr: Selection obscures the treated outcome of an always-selected individual even in a randomized trial, while marginal validity permits the error budget to concentrate in a rare cell. At an explicit two-cell law with target mass \(0.1\), central-score interval lotteries have robust oracle length \(0.09+0.9(h-0.1)_+\). On a declared seven-coordinate fixed-support neighborhood inside a public-floor subclass of Lee's model, every exactly honest observed-data rule incurs a positive root-\(n\) oracle-relative learning cost. An explicitly calibrated rule is exactly honest on that subclass and attains the root-\(n\) rate, with proved worst local constant \((9/10)\sqrt{9/8}/\sqrt{2\pi}\), approximately \(0.380828\). The converse also applies to procedures honest on the encompassing Lee class under the same action and loss criterion. The exact minimax constant and any sharp gain from using the full trial record remain open.
gap: Lee identifies predictive score-tail uncertainty and a reduced-information scalar cutoff. These results do not quantify the expected length cost of learning a randomized full-observed-law allocation when one selected stratum exhausts marginal error capacity.
fill: The oracle reduction, finite-experiment likelihood certificate, and augmented-count calibration jointly establish the root-\(n\) cost. An exact positive-part representation supplies a finite-sample upper bound, while the sharp constant question preserves the unresolved concentrating-action problem.
